newsitem.title: USA: EPA awards $16 mln contract to clean tainted NJ soil.
newsitem.headline: EPA awards $16 mln contract to clean tainted NJ soil.

text.p: The Environmental Protection Agency announced Wednesday it was awarding a $16 million contract to scoop radium-contaminated soil from residential properties in New Jersey.

The EPA's regional administrator, Jeanne Fox, said in a statement that the two-year contract went to Sevenson Environmental Services of Niagara Falls, N.Y., and would cover 59 properties in Orange and neigboring South Orange.

The project will cost $28 million when disposal is included. It is part of a continuing federal Superfund effort to compensate for the practices of the now defunct U.S. Radium Corporation here, which from 1917 to 1926 disposed of its waste sands by offering it for use as construction fill.
The sands contained small amounts of radium, which can be dangerous when it decays into radon gas, particularly if it accumulates in cellars or tightly insulated houses.
A total of 383 properties are on the Superfund watch list and 56 of them are slated for cleanup in the next phase, Fox said. The last stage will involve cleaning up the plant site.
Superfund projects are 90 percent paid for by federal funds and 10 percent by the state.
